en: The Apadāna of the Elder Reṇupūjaka Bhikkhadāyivagga, Number 10 [Verse 1] "Having offered a handful of dust to the Buddha, the Teacher, the One with Vision, the Knower of All Worlds, the One Who Has Transcended All Suffering, may I become a Buddha in this world. [Verse 2] Through that root of merit, having performed that deed, I was reborn in the world of the gods; after passing away from there, I was reborn among humans. [Verse 3] In whatever realm I was reborn, wherever I went, I was always honored by the people, like a heap of dust. [Verse 4] For eighty-four thousand aeons I experienced the fruit of that deed; having passed through those aeons, I attained the state of a Buddha. [Verse 5] I am the Buddha named Reṇu, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Fully Enlightened One; I have crossed over the ocean of existence and am now liberated from all suffering. [Verse 6] This is my own account of past deeds, accomplished by me in former lives; having heard it, one should practice the Dhamma, for the wise do not grieve. [Verse 7] May you all be well and happy; may you live long and free from disease; may you attain the highest peace, Nibbāna, which is the cessation of all suffering. Thus ends the Apadāna of the Elder Reṇupūjaka.
“The Sambuddha, golden-hued like the sun with its hundred rays,
illuminating all directions— ”
Like the full moon surrounded by the stars,
or like Mount Meru surrounded by the oceans, he was honored by his disciples.
Taking up dust from the nāga,
I offered it to Vipassi.
Ninety-one aeons ago,
The dust that I offered then—
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
In the forty-fifth aeon,
there was a kshatriya named Reṇu,
who was endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Reṇupūjaka spoke these verses.
This is the tenth legend of the elder Reṇupūjaka.
The eleventh chapter, the Bhikkhadāyivagga.
Its summary (uddāna) is:
Bhikkhadāyī, Ñāṇasaññī, ...
Hatthiya was the one who performed the foot-worship;
Muṭṭhipupphi offered flowers with his fist;
Udakada offered water; Naḷamāli was the attendant.
The Biḷālidāyī, the Reṇu,
and sixty verses.
